physicalNotes: Radius 0.23820145 Jupiter radii from Schlieder et al. 2016 (2016ApJ...818...87S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...818...87S/abstract): 17,029.5 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0239 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Beichman et al. 2016 (2016ApJ...822...39B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BEICHMAN_ET_AL__2016): P 14.568101 d
sources.shape: Schlieder et al. 2016 (2016ApJ...818...87S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SCHLIEDER_ET_AL__2016): a/R* 20.7; Schlieder et al. 2016 (2016ApJ...818...87S), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname SCHLIEDER_ET_AL__2016): inclination 88.4 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Beichman et al. 2016 (2016ApJ...822...39B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BEICHMAN_ET_AL__2016): transit mid-time 2456775.16503 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 8 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
